abiathar.title: Abiathar
abiathar.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
abiathar.note: He was the only priest to get out of Nob alive when Saul had the place killed, and he went straight to David and stayed his priest through the running years and the reign. At the end he backed Adonijah instead of Solomon, and Solomon sent him away from the priesthood rather than kill him.

abigal.title: Abigal
abigal.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
abigal.note: A variant spelling of Abigail, David's wife. She rode out to stop David wiping out her first husband Nabal's household, and it worked. Once Nabal was dead she married David.

abinadab-2.title: Abinadab
abinadab-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab-2.note: The man whose house held the ark. It sat there twenty years before David came for it.

abishai.title: Abishai
abishai.about: David's warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
abishai.note: David's nephew, and the most willing man he had. He is credited with three hundred killed on his own. Twice he offered to finish one of David's enemies on the spot, Saul asleep in the camp and Shimei cursing on the road, and both times David told him no.

abishalom.title: Abishalom
abishalom.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
abishalom.note: This is Absalom, David's third son. He killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, and when David punished neither of them he spent years quietly building support before taking the throne by force. The revolt ended with his famous hair caught in an oak while he was still riding.

abital.title: Abital
abital.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
abital.note: The fifth wife on David's list, and the mother of Shephatiah, who was born while David was still ruling from Hebron.

abner.title: Abner
abner.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
abner.note: Saul's cousin, and the commander of his army. When Saul died he did not stop: he kept the war going between David and what was left of Saul's house.

adonijah.title: Adonijah
adonijah.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
adonijah.note: David's fourth son. With his older brothers dead, he was the presumed heir. He tried to have himself crowned while David was still dying, and left Solomon, Nathan and Benaiah off the invitation.

ahilud.title: Ahilud
ahilud.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahilud.note: Two of his sons served kings: Jehoshaphat was David's royal recorder, and Baana governed one of Solomon's twelve districts.

ahimelech-2.title: Ahimelech
ahimelech-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimelech-2.note: A priest in David's time, named in the list at 2 Samuel 8:17 and in the priestly divisions of 1 Chronicles 24. He is not the priest of Nob, who belongs to Saul's years.

ahinoam.title: Ahinoam
ahinoam.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
ahinoam.note: The Ahinoam from Jezreel whom David married, mother of his firstborn son Amnon, and a different woman from Saul's wife of the same name.

ahio.title: Ahio
ahio.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahio.note: He and his brother Uzzah were guiding the cart that carried the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem. Uzzah reached out to steady it and was struck dead.

ahitub-2.title: Ahitub
ahitub-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahitub-2.note: Zadok's father, named in the list of officials at 2 Samuel 8:17 and in the priestly genealogy of Chronicles.

aiah.title: Aiah
aiah.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
aiah.note: A father named to place his daughter. Rizpah was one of Saul's concubines, and Aiah's only part is to say whose daughter she was.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

ammah.title: Ammah
ammah.note: A hill east of Gibeon. Joab and Abishai reached it at sunset chasing Abner after the fight at the pool of Gibeon, and there Abner called out to Joab and the two agreed a truce.

ammiel.title: Ammiel
ammiel.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ammiel.note: 1 Chronicles 3:5 makes an Ammiel the father of Bathsheba, called Bath-shua there. The name also turns up in 2 Samuel 9 and 17, given only as a father's name.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amnon.title: Amnon
amnon.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
amnon.note: David's firstborn. He raped his half-sister Tamar, with a cousin's scheme to help him, and David did not punish him. Two years later her full brother Absalom had Amnon murdered, and that was the start of the road to Absalom's revolt.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

aram-zobah.title: Aram-zobah
aram-zobah.note: An Aramean kingdom under its king Hadadezer. David beat it in a series of campaigns, pushed Israel's borders out, and brought home heavy tribute.

asahel.title: Asahel
asahel.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
asahel.note: Joab's younger brother, one of David's best warriors and famous for his speed. He died chasing Abner in the fighting between David's side and Saul's. Joab later murdered Abner for it, and that killing hung over David's reign.

ashkelon.title: Ashkelon
ashkelon.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, a port on the coast midway between Gaza and Joppa. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager. It is named on the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC.

asshurim.title: Asshurim
asshurim.note: One of the regions Abner made Ish-bosheth king over after Saul's death, with Gilead, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin. Assyria was far beyond Israel's reach then, so most read it as a scribal slip for Asherites, the land of Asher.

baal-perazim.title: Baal-perazim
baal-perazim.note: David named it, lord of breakthroughs more or less, after beating the Philistines there early in his reign over all Israel and comparing the win to floodwater breaking through.

baale-of-judah.title: Baale of Judah
baale-of-judah.note: The name 2 Samuel 6:2 uses for Kiriath-jearim, where the ark stayed for years before David brought it up to Jerusalem.

baanah.title: Baanah
baanah.about: David's compatriots living at the time of United Monarchy
baanah.note: He and his brother Rechab murdered Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul who was still alive, thinking David would thank them. David had them executed for killing an innocent man in his own bed.

bahurim.title: Bahurim
bahurim.note: A village east of Jerusalem, on the road down to the Jordan Valley. Shimei the Benjamite lived there. When David fled during Absalom's revolt, Shimei came out to curse him and throw stones.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

beeroth.title: Beeroth
beeroth.note: It was one of four Hivite cities, with Gibeon, Chephirah and Kiriath-jearim. Their people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by dressing up as travellers from far away. Later it was allotted to Benjamin.

beerothite.title: Beerothite
beerothite.note: Someone from Beeroth, a town of the Gibeonite league that Joshua had spared. Rechab and Baanah were Beerothites, the two officers who killed Saul's son Ish-bosheth and were executed by David for it.

benaiah.title: Benaiah
benaiah.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
benaiah.note: He commanded David's bodyguard, and before that he was known for killing a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He also beat an Egyptian giant by wrestling the giant's own spear off him and killing him with it.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

berothah.title: Berothah
berothah.note: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, owned this town, and David took a great deal of bronze from it after beating him. Samuel calls it Berothai. Ezekiel later names it alongside Hamath and Damascus.

betah.title: Betah
betah.note: One of Hadadezer's cities in Zobah, which David plundered for a large haul of bronze after beating the Aramean king.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bithron.title: Bithron
bithron.note: Abner and his men marched through it by night on their way back to Mahanaim, after Asahel was killed chasing Abner. It was a district or ravine in the Jordan Valley on the east side of the river.

carmelite.title: Carmelite
carmelite.note: Here it means someone from Carmel in Judah's hill country, not Mount Carmel in the north. Nabal was a Carmelite, the rich fool who insulted David, and so was his wife Abigail, who married David after Nabal died.

cherethims.title: Cherethims
cherethims.about: A military group in the Old Testament
cherethims.note: David's bodyguard, with the Pelethites, under Benaiah's command. They were tied closely to the Philistines and likely came from Crete.

chileab-2.title: Chileab
chileab-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
chileab-2.note: David's second son, by Abigail, born after Nabal died and David married her. Chronicles calls him Daniel. After the birth notice he never appears again, and since he plays no part in the fight over who would succeed David, he is generally thought to have died young.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

eglah.title: Eglah
eglah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
eglah.note: One of David's wives in his Hebron years, mother of Ithream. She appears only in those two lists.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

eliada.title: Eliada
eliada.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
eliada.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem.

eliphalet.title: Eliphalet
eliphalet.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
eliphalet.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, a name David used more than once.

elishama-2.title: Elishama
elishama-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
elishama-2.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, in the lists of 2 Samuel 5 and 1 Chronicles 3 and 14.

elishua.title: Elishua
elishua.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
elishua.note: Born to David in Jerusalem, and listed as Elishama in 1 Chronicles 3.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

gaba-3.title: Gaba
gaba-3.note: Named once, in 2 Samuel, and nowhere else.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gazer.title: Gazer
gazer.note: The same city as Gezer. Pharaoh took it and gave it to his daughter when she married Solomon, and Solomon fortified it along with Hazor and Megiddo. The Gezer Calendar, a little tablet of farming seasons in early Hebrew script, was found there.

geshur.title: Geshur
geshur.note: It was a small Aramean kingdom northeast of Galilee, and Absalom ran there after murdering his brother Amnon and stayed three years under his grandfather the king.

giah.title: Giah
giah.note: It exists in the record only to locate the hill of Ammah, where Joab gave up chasing Abner in the war between the houses of David and Saul. Its site has never been identified.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gilboa.title: Gilboa
gilboa.note: Saul died on these hills above the Jezreel Valley. The Philistines broke his army, three of his sons fell, Jonathan among them, and Saul, badly wounded, took his own life. David's lament curses Gilboa never to have dew or rain.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gittite.title: Gittite
gittite.note: A man from Gath. Obed-edom the Gittite kept the ark in his house before David brought it up to Jerusalem, and Ittai the Gittite brought his foreign troops to David's side when Absalom rebelled.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. The personal name is the four Hebrew letters YHWH, printed LORD in small capitals in most English Bibles; Jehovah is a later hybrid of those letters with the vowels of another word.

hadadezer.title: Hadadezer
hadadezer.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
hadadezer.note: David fought this Aramean king in campaign after campaign, and the wins pushed Israel's borders out and brought in tribute and a great deal of captured bronze.

haggith.title: Haggith
haggith.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
haggith.note: She was one of David's wives and Adonijah's mother, and her son tried to take the throne while David was dying.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hanun.title: Hanun
hanun.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
hanun.note: David sent men to comfort him when his father died, and the Ammonite king shaved off half their beards and cut their clothes short. It started a full war between Israel and Ammon with its Aramean allies.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

helam.title: Helam
helam.note: East of the Jordan, where Joab led David's army against Hadadezer's Arameans under Shobach and broke them. After that the Arameans stopped helping the Ammonites. Nobody has fixed the site.

helkath-hazzurim.title: Helkath-hazzurim
helkath-hazzurim.note: Field of blades, roughly. By the pool of Gibeon twelve of Joab's men and twelve of Abner's killed each other in pairs, and it set off the battle between David's side and Ish-bosheth's.

hiram.title: Hiram
hiram.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
hiram.note: He was king of Tyre and a friend to both David and Solomon, sending cedar and craftsmen for David's palace and for the temple and keeping up the trade with Israel through both reigns.

ibhar.title: Ibhar
ibhar.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
ibhar.note: Born to David in Jerusalem, after he was king, and nothing more.

ish-bosheth.title: Ish-bosheth
ish-bosheth.about: Saul's son living at the time of United Monarchy
ish-bosheth.note: Saul's surviving son, whom Abner made king over Israel while David held only Judah. When Abner went over to David, two of Ish-bosheth's own captains killed him in his bed.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

ithream.title: Ithream
ithream.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
ithream.note: David's sixth son born at Hebron, by his wife Eglah, and the story never mentions him again.

japhia.title: Japhia
japhia.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
japhia.note: Born to David in Jerusalem, and sharing his name with a king of Lachish and a town of Zebulun.

jehoiada-2.title: Jehoiada
jehoiada-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoiada-2.note: Known through his son, the commander of David's bodyguard who carried out the killings after David's death, in Samuel and Kings.

jehoshaphat-2.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoshaphat-2.note: David's recorder, the official who kept the court's records, and he still held the post in the next reign.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jetheth.title: Jetheth
jetheth.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetheth.note: Edom had clan chiefs who came down from Esau, and Jetheth is listed with them.

jezreel.title: Jezreel
jezreel.note: A valley and town in northern Israel. Naboth's vineyard was there, the one Ahab and Jezebel stole, and it was there that Jehu wiped out Ahab's whole house. Hosea named one of his children Jezreel to say judgment was coming.

jezreel-4.title: Jezreel
jezreel-4.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

joab.title: Joab
joab.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
joab.note: David's nephew, and the commander of his army for most of the reign. He was loyal to what David needed rather than what David said: he arranged Uriah's death when asked, killed Absalom when told not to, and murdered Abner and Amasa under cover of friendship. David never forgave him. On David's word Solomon had Joab killed, even holding on to the altar.

jonathan.title: Jonathan
jonathan.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan.note: Saul's eldest son, heir to the throne, and David's friend. He made a covenant with David knowing it cost him the crown. Once, with only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and started a rout of the Philistine army. He died with Saul and two brothers on Mount Gilboa, and David's lament for him says his love was "surpassing the love of women."

joram-3.title: Joram
joram-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
joram-3.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

laish-2.title: Laish
laish-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
laish-2.note: 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

lo-debar.title: Lo-debar
lo-debar.note: A town where, in 2 Samuel 9, a lame son of the old royal house is found living in another man's home. Amos plays on its name, which sounds like "nothing."

maachah-2.title: Maachah
maachah-2.note: A small Aramean kingdom near Geshur, east of the Sea of Galilee. Israel never managed to drive it out.

maachah-5.title: Maachah
maachah-5.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
maachah-5.note: One of 10 women called Maachah. This one is a woman from the united kingdom, named twice in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles.

machir-2.title: Machir
machir-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
machir-2.note: Not Manasseh's son. This Machir kept a lame son of the old royal house in his home, and later brought supplies to a king running from his own son's revolt.

mahanaim.title: Mahanaim
mahanaim.note: "Two camps." Jacob met the angels of God here near the Jabbok River on his way home, and split his household in two before facing Esau. After Saul died, Ishbosheth ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim while David held Hebron, and years later David fled there himself from Absalom and heard there that his son was dead.

mephibosheth.title: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth.about: Jonathan's son living at the time of United Monarchy
mephibosheth.note: Jonathan's son, lame in both feet since his nurse dropped him running from the news that Saul and Jonathan were dead. Years later David found him, gave him back Saul's land and a seat at the king's table for Jonathan's sake. During Absalom's rebellion a servant accused him of disloyalty, and his grief and unkempt state when David came home suggest the charge was false.

metheg-ammah.title: Metheg-ammah
metheg-ammah.note: Roughly "the bridle of the mother city," a figure of speech for the Philistine city David brought under him. Chronicles says it outright: David took Gath and its towns.

micha-4.title: Micha
micha-4.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
micha-4.note: Mephibosheth had a young son called Micha, and that is the whole of what 2 Samuel 9:12 says.

michal.title: Michal
michal.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
michal.note: Saul's younger daughter. David won her by killing two hundred Philistines, and she saved his life by letting him down through a window when Saul's men came. Saul then gave her to another man; David took her back as king, but she despised him for dancing before the ark, and she had no children to the end of her life.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

nabal.title: Nabal
nabal.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nabal.note: A rich, hard man. David's men had guarded his shepherds, and when David asked for food Nabal sent back insults. Only his wife Abigail, riding out with a generous gift, kept David from killing his whole household. When she told Nabal ten days later what he had nearly brought on them, he seems to have had a stroke, and he died. David married Abigail.

nachon.title: Nachon
nachon.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
nachon.note: At the threshing floor of Nachon, Uzzah reached out to steady the ark and died. Chronicles calls it the threshing floor of Chidon, and scholars are split on whether that was one man with two names or whether one text named the place rather than its owner.

nahash-2.title: Nahash
nahash-2.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash-2.note: A king of the Ammonites. When he died, Israel's king sent men to comfort his son, and 2 Samuel 10 is the war that came out of how they were received.

nathan-2.title: Nathan
nathan-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan-2.note: One of David's sons born in Jerusalem. Luke traces Jesus' line through him, not through Solomon.

nathan.title: Nathan
nathan.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan.note: The prophet who told David the story of the rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, let David condemn the man, and then turned it on him over Bathsheba and Uriah. Earlier he had brought God's promise that David's house would last forever. When David was dying, Nathan helped put Solomon on the throne ahead of a rival half-brother.

nepheg.title: Nepheg
nepheg.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
nepheg.note: One of David's sons born in Jerusalem, and nothing more is told of him.

ner.title: Ner
ner.about: Saul's uncle living at the time of United Monarchy
ner.note: Father of Abner, Saul's army commander. Ner was Saul's grandfather or great-uncle, depending on how the genealogies are fitted together.

obed-edom.title: Obed-edom
obed-edom.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
obed-edom.note: After Uzzah died, David would not take the ark any further and left it in Obed-edom's house for three months. It brought blessing on his whole household, and that was what got David moving again.

paltiel.title: Paltiel
paltiel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
paltiel.note: Two men. One was the leader from Issachar picked to help divide the land among the tribes. The other, son of Laish, was given Michal by King Saul after David fled, and he lost her again when David took her back.

pelethites.title: Pelethites
pelethites.note: They always come paired with the Cherethites, as David's personal guard under Benaiah. The names sound foreign, and they were probably hired soldiers of Philistine or Aegean background.

perezuzza.title: Perezuzza
perezuzza.note: The breach of Uzzah. David gave the threshing floor this name after Uzzah reached out to steady the ark and was struck dead.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

rechab-2.title: Rechab
rechab-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
rechab-2.note: He and his brother were captains of raiding bands. They killed their own master in his bed, carried the head off expecting a reward, and were put to death for it.

rehob.title: Rehob
rehob.note: The far edge of the spies' route into Canaan, up in the north. Asher was allotted a Rehob too, and Judges 1:31 says Asher never drove out the people living there.

rehob-2.title: Rehob
rehob-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
rehob-2.note: 2 Samuel names him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

remmon.title: Remmon
remmon.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
remmon.note: Father of the two captains who murdered their master in his bed (2 Samuel 4:2), and he is named for no other reason.

rizpah.title: Rizpah
rizpah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
rizpah.note: Saul's concubine. When David handed seven of Saul's descendants over to be executed to end a famine, two of them her sons, she kept watch over their bodies for months. She drove off the birds by day and the animals by night.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

seraiah-7.title: Seraiah
seraiah-7.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
seraiah-7.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

shammua.title: Shammua
shammua.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
shammua.note: One of David's sons, named in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4. Nehemiah 11:17 has the name again for a later man.

shephatiah-2.title: Shephatiah
shephatiah-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
shephatiah-2.note: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

shobab.title: Shobab
shobab.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
shobab.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem after he became king.

shobach.title: Shobach
shobach.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
shobach.note: He led Hadadezer's army and brought in troops from beyond the Euphrates to fight for the Ammonites against David. Joab's men killed him at Helam. After that the Arameans backed off.

sirah.title: Sirah
sirah.note: Joab's men called Abner back from the well of Sirah, north of Hebron, after David had let him go in peace. Then Joab killed him, in revenge for his brother.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

talmai.title: Talmai
talmai.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
talmai.note: A king of Geshur, whose daughter Maacah married David and bore Absalom.

tob.title: Tob
tob.note: Jephthah's half-brothers drove him out for being a prostitute's son, and he went to the land of Tob, east of Gilead. He gathered outlaws there until Gilead's elders came to fetch him back to fight the Ammonites. Men of Tob later hired themselves out to the Ammonites.

toi.title: Toi
toi.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
toi.note: King of Hamath. When David beat Hadadezer, who had been at war with Toi, Toi sent his son with gold, silver and bronze to congratulate him.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uzza.title: Uzza
uzza.note: Uzzah put his hand out to steady the ark when the oxen stumbled, and he died on the spot. David was afraid, and the ark stayed where it was for three months before it went on to Jerusalem.

zadok.title: Zadok
zadok.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
zadok.note: The priest who stayed with David through Absalom's rebellion. He would have carried the ark out with the king, and David sent it back. Zadok anointed Solomon, and when Abiathar backed Adonijah and was sent away, Zadok was left as the only high priest.

zeruiah.title: Zeruiah
zeruiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
zeruiah.note: David's sister, the mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel. David said the sons of Zeruiah were too much for him.

ziba.title: Ziba
ziba.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
ziba.note: A servant of Saul's house. David put him in charge of Mephibosheth's land, and during Absalom's rebellion Ziba told David that Mephibosheth had turned against him. It was a lie, and it cost Mephibosheth half his property.

ziklag.title: Ziklag
ziklag.note: Achish of Gath gave this town in the Negev to David while he was running from Saul, and David lived there more than a year. Amalekites burned it while he was away and took the women and children, and he went after them and got everyone back.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.

zoba.title: Zoba
zoba.note: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus. Saul fought it, David beat its king Hadadezer and took his chariots and his bronze, and a man from Zobah named Rezon troubled Solomon from Damascus.
